items: Stress is real but contained; this quarter's keyword is differentiation, not collapse. Four of the five sell-side houses are neutral-to-constructive; UBS is the only outright bear. Risk is concentrated in specific sectors and specific vintages rather than a system-wide event; banks' exposure to private credit is only ~3% of their loan books.

Software is the epicentre, and has shifted from sector-wide repricing to single-name differentiation. Software is ~26% of BDC collateral. Realised defaults are just 2.3% (vs 5.7% across all asset classes) — the panic is not yet validated by the data — but implied recovery of ~48pts is low, and Medallia's hand-over to lenders is the first live test case.

The 2028 maturity wall hasn't shrunk — it has been pushed back. ~US$80bn matures in each of 2028–2030; this quarter the 2031–33 bucket grew from ~US$194bn to US$207bn while 2026–27 maturities fell — amend-and-extend is deferring the problem, not solving it. Non-accrual balances from 2021–22 vintages run ~3x the 2024 vintage: the wall is landing on the weakest cohort.

This may be the best deployment window of the cycle on terms. Redemption-pressured non-traded BDCs have cut hold sizes sharply and pulled back from software; reduced competition has widened spreads 25–50bp with documentation and LTVs improving in step. Retail is only ~20% of private credit AUM, and institutional money is returning.

No warning signals across our three funds this quarter, but marks lag secondary prints. All are valued as of 31 Mar 2026 and do not yet reflect Q2's public-market repricing of software and private credit. Private credit secondaries are now at scale (JPMorgan ~US$2bn traded, par to –10pts).
Global private debt AUM US$2,557bn (institutional 77%); the US leveraged credit market is US$4.4tn, of which private credit US$1.4tn (32%), with BDCs holding 38% of that.

Supply is contracting: dry powder of US$618.2bn is past peak; 2025 fundraising of US$221.2bn across 206 funds is down 30% / 60% from the 2021 peaks. The growth model has shifted from “fundraising-driven” to “deploying the stock”.

Demand: volumes down, pricing steady. Private credit still finances 80–83% of LBOs, but 2026 YTD new lending is ~US$87bn (–24% YoY), with Q2 at just US$33bn / 149 deals (Q1: US$74.1bn / 217) — the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz closure froze M&A — while refinancing holds steady at ~40% of volume.

Returns: private debt annualised 7.8% from 2015 to Mar-26 with 2.2% volatility and a 3.6 Sharpe — but fair-value smoothing flatters this, and correlation with BSL is 82.4%. Direct lending LTM return 8.7% (−2.2pp YoY).

Pricing: unitranche new-issue spread 508bp vs 430bp for single-B BSL — a ~78bp premium that has stopped compressing and is turning wider. Terms keep stratifying: only ~37% of 2024-vintage upper-middle-market deals carry a financial covenant (54% in 2021), and the share with PIK toggles has risen to ~41%.

items: PAG BRS III: subscription-line financing at 62%; exited Veleta in Q1 at a 12% unlevered IRR, distributing US$59mn. Below-median TVPI is the early-distribution signature of an SRT strategy — DPI at P72 cross-validates.

Guggenheim PDF IV: final close completed at the US$4.5bn hard cap (+50% vs initial target); 39 of 40 investments performing, 1 on the watch list, no non-accruals; software ~17% vs the industry's ~26%. Last six deals at SOFR+546bp, first-lien net leverage 4.0x, blended LTV 42% — confirming the improvement in terms.
HSBC RCF: watch list empty, all 11 live positions green; pro forma size ~€435mn.
Review software exposure name by name, not just by sector weight — this cycle's differentiation is at the issuer level, not the sector level.
In new-fund diligence and existing-manager reviews, require non-accrual and PIK metrics split by vintage as standard — vintage has become the most important stratification variable.
Cross-check our three funds' quarterly marks against available secondary-market prints, especially on software exposure.
Use the current deployment window, while treating 2028 as the cycle's pivotal year in duration and refinancing-risk management.
Amend-and-extend share and the share of PIK-term amendments — the earliest signals of “liquidity problems” turning into “payment problems”, ahead of default rates themselves.
Whether BDC non-accruals stabilise within 3%, and whether the ~2.5pp listed vs non-traded gap converges as vintages season.

From 2026Q4, quartile migration and interquartile width in the benchmark set: 2023-vintage IRR dispersion has reached 4.6pp (2021 vintage: only 2.1pp), while 2024-vintage TVPI dispersion of just 0.04x has yet to open up — watch when AI/software repricing feeds through to fund marks.
Timing of the recovery in M&A and sponsor exit activity — it directly drives our repayment pace and DPI curves.
